reference_cards.title: Quantifier scope
reference_cards.guidance: Preserve quantifier order and allow later witnesses to depend only on information already quantified.

reference_cards.title: Cancellation domains
reference_cards.guidance: Record domains and prove a factor nonzero before cancelling it from an equation or expression.

reference_cards.title: Branches after squaring
reference_cards.guidance: A square root of a square gives an absolute value; retain sign branches and recheck candidates.

reference_cards.title: Induction reachability
reference_cards.guidance: An induction stride reaches only residue classes connected to the supplied base cases.

reference_cards.title: Index regions
reference_cards.guidance: When sums are swapped, preserve the same lattice region and derive every dependent boundary.

reference_cards.title: Matrix size notions
reference_cards.guidance: Keep spectral radius, eigenvalues, singular values, operator norm, and rank as distinct quantities.

reference_cards.title: Local versus global control
reference_cards.guidance: Radial or coordinate-axis control does not by itself establish a global Lipschitz estimate.

reference_cards.title: Feasible boundaries
reference_cards.guidance: Optimize over the full feasible set, including origins and faces, and distinguish balls from spheres.

reference_cards.title: Multiplicity and scale
reference_cards.guidance: Retain combinatorial multiplicity and distinguish an exact count, a bound, and an asymptotic rate.

reference_cards.title: Both implications
reference_cards.guidance: An equivalence needs each implication; proving one direction cannot establish the reverse direction.

reference_cards.title: Modular cancellation
reference_cards.guidance: Cancelling a modular factor can change the modulus unless that factor is invertible there.

reference_cards.title: Candidate replay
reference_cards.guidance: Replay transformed candidates in the original equation and enforce every original domain condition.

reference_cards.title: Overlap correction
reference_cards.guidance: Inclusion-exclusion corrects overlap so each object contributes exactly once to the union.

reference_cards.title: Coprimality hypotheses
reference_cards.guidance: Divisibility cancellation requires the correct coprimality or primality hypothesis before drawing a conclusion.

reference_cards.title: Rank and nullity
reference_cards.guidance: Rank-nullity uses the domain dimension; rank is not merely a count of nonzero eigenvalues.

reference_cards.title: Mutual independence
reference_cards.guidance: Marginals or pairwise independence do not establish mutual independence of the full collection.

reference_cards.title: Sign cases
reference_cards.guidance: Variable-sign inequality operations require separate interval cases around every zero and pole.

reference_cards.title: Initial data sufficiency
reference_cards.guidance: A recurrence needs as many independent initial values as its order before forward replay is unique.

reference_cards.title: Aggregate versus pointwise
reference_cards.guidance: An aggregate parity, average, or sum statement does not imply the corresponding pointwise statement.

reference_cards.title: Polynomial sample threshold
reference_cards.guidance: A bounded-degree polynomial identity needs enough distinct samples to force the difference polynomial to vanish.
